description: A DNS server that takes dynamic updates, RFC 2136, as BIND, Knot and PowerDNS do, and Windows DNS where it allows nonsecure updates: the primary of the zone. Each update replaces the name's A and AAAA records in one step, over TCP, and leaves its records of other types. Without a TSIG key, the server must take updates from the address of the machine ipv6ddns runs on. Give ipv6ddns a zone of its own, not one a DHCP server registers its clients in: both would write the same names.

server.description: The primary server of the zone, as 192.168.1.2 or ns1.example.com:53. Without a port, 53.

tsig_key.description: The name of the TSIG key the updates are signed with, as ipv6ddns. Leave it out for a server that takes updates by address.

tsig_secret.description: The key's secret, in base64, as tsig-keygen gives it.
